newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Old Russian oil fields could see output recover.
newsitem.headline: Old Russian oil fields could see output recover.

text.p: Many Russian oil fields are past their prime but could see production improvement if new technology was applied, production recovery specialist Stanislav Zhdanov said on Tuesday.
"The problem faced by Russia's oil industry today is that the majority of the fields are mature," Zhdanov, an expert in optimising oil recovery at Russia's Nefteotdacha, told an industry conference.
But he said improved technology could boost output.

"Under favourable conditions, oil recovery in Russia could rise by the year 2000 by a total of 10-20 million tonnes (200,000 to 400,000 barrels per day, or bpd), by using new, more efficient means of development," he said.
Russia produced 293 million tonnes (5.86 million bpd) of oil in 1996, down around two percent from 1995 levels.
Zhdanov said production from difficult-to-access oil reserves accounted for about half Russian production and predicted that figure would grow.
He also said reactivating idle wells was another way of boosting output, although the longer the delay in restarting the wells the greater the eventual loss in output from any field.
"Russia has quite a few idle wells now -- around 40,000," he said. "They are not coming back on stream because of the lack of financing, which is leading to a loss in production," he said.
